title: Karnataka Requires Night-Time Attendance for Doctors at Taluk Hospitals, PHCs
excerpt: From November 1, doctors must record their presence after 9 p.m. through the geo-fencing Kartavya app within their headquarters area, as Karnataka extends app-based attendance to contract staff with pay linked from January 1, 2027.
body:
• From November 1, 2026, doctors at Karnataka taluk hospitals and primary health centres must record their night-time presence after 9 p.m. through the geo-fencing-based Kartavya mobile app, within their designated headquarters area.
  • The order, issued by Principal Secretary Harsh Gupta with the Chief Minister's approval, follows an Upalokayukta inquiry finding that several government employees were not residing at their headquarters.
  • Leave, official duty outside headquarters, and prior permission to leave are exempt — but the reason must be recorded in the app; commissioners and district health officers review reports monthly, and unpermitted absence can bring disciplinary action.
  • The same app becomes mandatory for contract and outsourced staff across all departments: registration by November 25, exclusive recording from December 1, and pay linked to app attendance from January 1, 2027.

Karnataka has made night-time attendance mandatory for doctors working at taluk hospitals and primary health centres (PHCs), requiring them to record their presence after 9 p.m. each day through the geo-fencing-based Kartavya mobile application.

The system comes into force on November 1, 2026, for doctors under the Health and Family Welfare Department, according to The Hindu. A doctor complies only by recording attendance through the app while inside the geographical limits of the town or village designated as their headquarters — the order is about residing at the place of posting, not simply about marking a shift.

Why the Government Issued the Order

The order was issued by Harsh Gupta, Principal Secretary of the Praja Seva Department, with the Chief Minister's approval. It follows observations during an inquiry by the Upalokayukta that several government employees were not residing at their designated headquarters and were instead managing their duties from distant places. That had resulted in delays in reporting for work and inconvenience to the public, the order stated.

The government said the pilot is intended to improve compliance with service rules and to ensure officials are available to meet the public's needs. For taluk hospitals and PHCs, availability at night is the core service question: these are the first government facilities most rural patients reach, and a doctor who lives elsewhere cannot respond to a night emergency at the facility.

Exemptions and Enforcement

Employees on sanctioned leave are exempt. Exemptions also apply to those on official duty outside their headquarters with the approval of the competent authority, and to those who have obtained prior permission to leave their headquarters. In each case, the reason for the leave or permission must be clearly recorded in the app.

Commissioners and district health officers must review night-attendance reports every month. Employees found not residing at their designated headquarters without permission may face disciplinary action under the applicable civil service rules. Based on the pilot's results, the Kartavya-based system may be extended to employees in other government departments and cadres.

The Wider Kartavya Rollout

The doctors' order sits inside a broader shift of Karnataka government attendance onto the Kartavya app. As HRKatha reported earlier this year, the state made geo-tagged attendance through the Karnataka Attendance Management System mandatory for government employees, with the HRMS attendance feature incorporated into the Kartavya app, after biometric devices in several offices became ineffective or were allegedly misused. That system was initially piloted in the Health Department before being expanded.

The latest orders extend the same logic in two directions at once. Night-time recording tests whether health staff actually live at their headquarters, and, under a separate circular also approved by the Chief Minister, contract and outsourced employees in all government departments, offices, boards, corporations, authorities and government-aided institutions must now record attendance through Kartavya as well. Department heads must ensure all such employees register on the app by November 25, 2026; from December 1, their attendance must be recorded exclusively through the app; and from January 1, 2027, contract employees' salaries and outsourcing agencies' bills will be released only on the basis of attendance reports generated by the app. Drawing and Disbursing Officers have been instructed not to release payments where attendance has not been recorded, and department heads will be held personally responsible for lapses in implementing the order, Mr. Gupta said in the circular.

What Doctors Should Do Now

Doctors at taluk hospitals and PHCs have until November 1 to be registered on Kartavya and able to record from within their headquarters limits after 9 p.m. Those who need to be away — on leave, on duty elsewhere, or with permission — should ensure the reason is recorded in the app in advance, because an unrecorded absence is what the monthly review and disciplinary provisions are built to catch.
